Jetson physical A/B update and rollback, audit2341

All cases start not_run. Generation reads local files and the pinned updater
checkout. It does not contact, update, reboot or recover any device. Run separate
inventories and complete evidence for Orin/tegra234 and Thor/tegra264; one cannot
qualify the other. The test changes BOTH rootfs slots over its complete sequence.
Use only a reserved disposable board, serial @SERIAL@, with its named owner.

Preparation and exact target

1. Reserve the actual module/carrier, recovery ECID, serial-console endpoint,
   storage model/serial/capacity and GPT. Record module/carrier revision, UEFI
   version, L4T release and kernel. Match the public Agent principal/key and direct
   management endpoint to the same physical serial. Do not select by IP alone.
   Keep independent serial console, wired management, stable power and the exact
   owner-reviewed recovery image/flashpack plus backup. The recovery_record must
   contain hashes, board-specific button/cable sequence, storage fingerprint,
   backup restoration instructions and a named person able to recover THIS board.
   No shared/production app, model or container is to be removed for this test.
   The owner must authorize the complete reserved-board OTA/reboot/rollback
   sequence separately from generating it. Record that authorization privately.

2. Inventory fields: board {device_type,soc,storage,serial,device_tree_serial,ecid,
   owner,carrier,root_disk_serial,firmware,l4t,address,initial_slot,app_partuuid,
   app_b_partuuid,esp_partuuid,redundancy:{attributes,value},retries:{attributes,
   value}}; install_seconds,boot_seconds; trial (32 random hex characters);
   cli_revision,agent_revision (full commits); cli_binary,agent_binary,
   updater_binary,updater_source,identity_record,recovery_record,authorization_record;
   artifacts.normal and artifacts.reject each contain archive,descriptor,
   payload_inspection paths. All record paths must identify existing local files.
   Use the candidate Agent containing the compatibility fix and the exact pinned
   updater1f160d407833783755af153a64f1b386e8f922ac. Hash the installed binaries, not
   just version strings. On the host run:
     python3 jetson-ab-rehearsal.py inventory.json NEW_PRIVATE_OUTPUT
   The generated commands pin the direct target, candidate Agent binary and exact
   artifact URL. Do not add --json to device update: it suppresses OS updates and
   is incompatible with --artifact-url. Do not substitute `os update`: that verb
   can fetch a different latest Agent before installing the image.

3. Prepare TWO actual board/storage-specific rootfs-only .wendy images through the
   existing reviewed producer, with different artifact names/versions. Both must
   contain the pinned candidate Agent and updater. The reject image differs by
   the unique executable /@HOOK@, whose bytes must equal generated health-reject.sh:
   it prints CI2341_HEALTH_REJECT @TRIAL@ and exits1. It performs no other action.
   Include that hook in the BUILT reject image, never in the running origin image.
   Normal image has no such hook. Do not overwrite or remove existing health hooks.
   Verify every production health hook remains present in both images and runnable.
   No capsule marker may exist in either image. bootloader_update in manifest.json
   is informational; inspect the actual rootfs marker path. This procedure does
   not qualify capsule updates or physical power-cut durability.

   Each producer descriptor records url,sha256,size_bytes,storage,artifact_name,
   artifact_version. Use immutable HTTPS paths without credential queries or
   moving latest/nightly aliases; reserve the exact objects against replacement.
   Compare the full local archive hash with the published producer result. The
   generator checks actual manifest board compatibility and stored payload digest.
   It does NOT decompress/mount the rootfs or verify the operator's inspection.
   Each payload_inspection JSON must be independently reviewed and bound to
   artifact_sha256,rootfs_sha256,agent_sha256,updater_sha256,
   bootloader_marker_present:false, health_hook_path, health_hook_mode and health_hook_sha256,
   reviewer. For normal, the health-hook fields are null; for reject mode is "0755" and they match
   the generated path and bytes. The inspection record must also describe the
   producer revision, complete health-hook inventory/modes, image read-only mount
   method, actual rootfs hash and firmware/L4T compatibility review. Do not sign off
   this record merely by copying fields from a manifest. V1 manifest.sig is reserved
   and unverified; it is not a signature/authenticity guarantee.

4. Use the generated info/status host commands. On the same physically identified
   board, through its local serial console, transfer the generated snapshot helper
   and snapshot-config.json by an owner-approved local method. Do not use SSH or
   broad remote shell access. First verify python3, util-linux findmnt/lsblk and GNU coreutils timeout are
   present on the board. Missing observer tools keep the case pending; do not
   install or replace target packages merely to manufacture a pass. Invoke
   explicitly as root, with the actually expected
   initial slot a or b:
     timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 180s python3 jetson-ab-snapshot.py snapshot-config.json --slot @ORIGIN@ > baseline.json
   The expected initial slot is @ORIGIN@, and the first target is @TARGET@. The helper refuses a different
   DT serial/SoC, device type, running root MAJ:MIN, GPT partition UUID, parent disk
   serial, updater hash or custom updater paths. APP, APP_b and ESP must share the
   reserved disk. Unsupported layouts need a separate plan, not relaxed checks.
   It records both nvbootctrl layers, raw EFI UINT32 attributes/values, live Agent
   executable hash, boot ID, updater status/check, public durable state and units.
   `status` may read-only mount the inactive slot, as specified by the updater.
   Compare nvbootctrl slot, actual mounted root and JSON current_slot; disagreement
   is a stop condition. Inspect /etc/nv_tegra_release and console UEFI banner against
   the firmware/L4T record. Preserve both successful and failing command exits.
   Never read private enrollment keys/tokens into evidence. Require the existing
   WendyOS to be at least 0.17.0 and already on the pinned .wendy engine family;
   a pre-0.17/Mender baseline needs separately authorized recovery/requalification.

5. Require no pending engine state, no Agent pending marker and a healthy origin
   before any install. The default engine state is /data/wendyos-update/state.json;
   history is installed.json. Locate the Agent's actual configuration directory
   from its unit/configuration and record only pending-update.json and
   last-update-result.json there, never the entire configuration or identity key.
   Snapshot helper deliberately does not assume that Agent directory. If an update
   is already pending, STOP. The readiness fix requires overall check success;
   stale-pending volatile-zero Orin recovery is still unfixed. Never delete state,
   mark-good, commit an unbooted image or fabricate an EFI value to make this pass.
   Resolve an existing incident under the separate recovery record, retain that
   failure, and start a fresh baseline only after independent review.

Case A: Agent OTA, actual slot switch and committed second boot

6. For the new Orin exception, require naturally observed volatile attributes0x06,
   redundancy0, retries1..3 and an overall successful pinned updater `check --json`
   with the named rootfs A/B redundancy check true. The legacy preparation would
   refuse this state, while the updater uses boot-chain A/B. For Thor, record actual
   level/retry state. Writable disabled NV attributes0x07 must be repaired and
   read back by the Agent before install; enabled settings must remain unchanged.
   A volatile disabled Thor level must be refused, not promoted to a successful
   OTA. If no genuine writable-disabled Thor state exists, leave the physical
   repair subcase not_run and run the ordinary enabled-state OTA separately.
   Do not unload drivers, write EFI variables, reflash unusual firmware or force
   values solely to manufacture the precondition.

7. Start a fresh serial transcript and bounded interval of Agent/updater journals
   before running update_normal on the host. Record start UTC/monotonic time,
   initial boot ID, initial mounted root/slot, old OS version and prior result
   timestamp. The command first installs the EXACT candidate Agent via --binary;
   require its restart/identity match and installed executable hash before crediting
   the subsequent OS result. Both artifact download and image manifest identities
   must match the reviewed producer object. Observe at most @INSTALL@ seconds for
   install plus @BOOT@ seconds for each reboot. This is a human observation bound,
   not permission to kill an active flash writer. If it expires, mark failure,
   retain console evidence, interrupt the host CLI once, and inspect the same board.
   Do not start a second writer, remove power, reboot or erase during an active
   write. Use the reserved recovery record if it cannot finish safely.

8. Require install progress through image verification and slot scheduling, then
   a real new boot ID on the opposite exact APP/APP_b partition. For Orin require
   the boot-chain slot to move; for Thor require the rootfs slot to move. Preserve
   both layer dumps, firmware banner and Agent/updater journals. A reconnected
   Agent alone is not success. Run status and a new console snapshot with
   --slot @TARGET@ --require-agent. Require the exact candidate image
   version, live Agent/updater hashes, root disk serial, same public device identity,
   successful commit, no pending state and a new installed.json entry containing
   this artifact name/version and actual slot. Compare the fresh Agent update result
   timestamp/outcome with this attempt; an older committed record is not evidence.
   If systemd committed first, record its fresh exit/result and engine history;
   an Agent 'nothing pending' response alone does not prove a commit.

9. After commitment, use the operator's local console `systemctl reboot` once.
   Within @BOOT@ seconds require another new boot ID, SAME committed slot/root,
   exact binaries/identity and healthy Agent RPC. Repeat snapshots/status. Require
   no pending state or unexpected rollback, and persisted EFI repair on a genuinely
   exercised Thor repair case. For Orin compare volatile level/retry observations
   without asserting a runtime EFI write occurred. This second boot is necessary
   to distinguish a persistent setting from a volatile value that happened to
   appear correct immediately after installation.

Case B: fresh target boot rejects health, then returns to the healthy origin

10. Treat the now committed normal image as the known healthy origin; capture its
    slot, boot ID, version, fresh history and state absence. Run update_reject with
    a new transcript. It must install to the opposite rootfs, boot that target and
    execute the exact nonce-bearing failing health hook. Use serial and boot-ID
    journals to prove the target actually booted. A failed download/preflight or a
    boot that never reached the hook does not satisfy this case. Do not manually
    run commit/rollback or alter hooks while the Agent's delegated health gate is
    active. Require real updater commit rejection, the Agent's automatic rollback
    decision, and its subsequent reboot to the original healthy slot. Allow the
    same @INSTALL@ install bound and at most two @BOOT@ reboot windows.

11. Require nonzero update-command result with rollback/health failure, plus fresh
    CLI status recording rolled-back outcome for THIS attempted artifact. After
    recovery, snapshot the expected origin slot with --require-agent. Require the
    prior healthy normal image version/hash/identity, actual origin root MAJ:MIN,
    no pending engine state, no installed-history entry committing the reject image,
    and the nonce hook failure in the target's retained journal/serial transcript.
    Capture the target boot ID and distinct returned-origin boot ID. Then reboot
    normally once more and require the same healthy origin and no repeated install
    or rollback loop. Missing early target-boot evidence keeps the automatic rollback
    case incomplete even if the board is healthy now. A diagnostic timeout, updater
    generic error, stale result or unrelated health failure is not the intended control.

Case C: explicit pre-reboot rollback of a staged rootfs update

12. This supplemental case tests the shipped updater directly and is not evidence
    that the Agent's preflight ran. On the recovered healthy origin, again require
    no pending state and no concurrent updater. With fresh exact-target approval,
    use the pinned binary on the local console to install the SAME normal artifact
    from its exact reviewed immutable URL:
      Run the exact generated console_install_normal command below.
    Do not reboot yet. This verb does not reboot. Use the same install observation
    bound, preserve stdout/stderr and exit status, and require phase done, the exact
    target/manifest and durable state phase swapped targeting the opposite slot.
    The current boot ID and mounted root must still be the healthy origin.
    Observe the state without invoking commit. Then run locally:
      /usr/bin/wendyos-update rollback
    Require exit0, JSON origin_slot equal to the still-running healthy origin,
    reboot_required:false, and state.json removed. Do not call switch or mark-good:
    they have different semantics and cannot substitute for rollback.
    Perform one normal console `systemctl reboot`; within @BOOT@ seconds require
    the same origin slot/image, new boot ID, no pending state and healthy identity.
    If another boot service unexpectedly commits while staging, stop and classify
    the attempt instead of creating/deleting state to force the test.

Payload digest evidence comes from producer bytes and successful installer
verification. A mounted filesystem changes during boot; do not compare its live
whole-partition hash with the pristine image and call that a stable image identity.
Use the exact booted partition, artifact receipts, version and live binary hashes.

Recovery and results

13. Preserve complete failed attempts before recovery. Restore only the reserved
    board and disk under the previously approved recovery record, using the known
    healthy producer artifact or exact board-specific recovery image. Never remove
    arbitrary EFI/state files, install a broad hook mask, or clean up production
    models/containers. The failing hook remains only in the rejected inactive lab
    image until an authorized replacement/recovery overwrites it. End with no
    pending state, normal health hooks, known healthy image on the required slots,
    the expected firmware/root disk and authenticated Agent status. Record exact
    restoration actions, hashes and any data restoration separately.

14. Keep inventory, producer/inspection records, generated source hashes, explicit
    authorization, all command exits, monotonic/UTC timestamps, serial output,
    before/after EFI bytes, both slot layers, mounted-root/GPT identity, engine
    state/history, fresh Agent receipts and complete boot-ID intervals. Independent
    review must connect them to the same physical serial and artifact. Mark a case
    passed only after ALL listed observations; missing capability, unsupported
    layout, unverified image/firmware or incomplete recovery remains not_run/failed
    as appropriate. No board operations are authorized or proven by generator tests.
